title: The Soldier’s Path: Basic Training for the Kingdom of God
description: Discipleship was never meant to be passive. The Soldier’s Path is a call to spiritual formation, disciplined surrender, and faithful living in the Kingdom of God. It invites believers to move beyond surface faith and into a life trained by truth, shaped by obedience, and strengthened for the journey with God.

title: The Path: A Journey to Sanctification
description: The Path follows the movement from striving and self-managed spirituality toward surrender, dependence, communion with God, and a life that grows from abiding rather than control. Through the image of two trees, it contrasts a life held together by effort with a life rooted in God. The journey explores breaking points, trust, hearing God, hidden formation, the dark night, refining, rest, and the stability of daily surrender.

title: Thy Kingdom Come
description: Thy Kingdom Come explores the Kingdom of God as a present reality, not merely a future destination. It examines what it means to live under the rule of the King now, allowing His reign to shape worship, obedience, relationships, purpose, and everyday life. The book challenges religious habits that can become detached from the Spirit and calls readers toward a lived relationship with God in which His Kingdom becomes visible through surrendered people.

title: God's Will, My Way
description: God’s Will, My Way is a personal exploration of the difference between moving quickly for God and actually moving with Him. Through stories of open doors, momentum, false urgency, resistance, surrender, and trust, the book asks whether success and movement are always evidence of obedience. It challenges the instinct to act first and seek God’s confirmation later, replacing the question “Is the door open?” with the deeper question, “Did God ask me to walk through it?”

title: The Sanctification Cycle
description: The Sanctification Cycle gives language to the deeper work of God that shakes, surrenders, stretches, secures, and seals a life. Moving through the stages of shaking, surrender, struggle, stretching, securing, and sealing, the book presents sanctification as more than moral improvement. It is the costly formation of a person who can carry what God entrusts to them. The book speaks especially to those who feel hidden, tested, refined, or prepared through difficult seasons.

title: AM I a Bad god?
description: AM I a Bad god? examines the quiet ways we learn to live as the center, chooser, judge, and author of our own lives. Culture trains us toward self-rule long before we recognize it, shaping our desires, identity, and definitions of freedom. The book asks what happens when God becomes an adviser rather than King and invites readers to lay down the burden of sovereignty, surrender the throne, and rediscover life in a Kingdom they were never meant to control.

title: The Ache
description: The Ache explores the longing beneath achievement, approval, relationships, comfort, control, and the many things we reach for when something inside us still feels unfinished. Rather than treating the ache as a defect to eliminate, the book considers what our deepest longings reveal about the way we were made. It invites readers to stop numbing or managing the hunger and begin tracing it back toward the God who alone can meet what the soul was created to receive.

title: The Awakening
description: The Awakening begins with the quiet realization that something no longer fits. A belief cracks, a system stops making sense, or a life built around comfort begins to feel like a cage. The book explores the subtle ways culture, institutions, expectations, and inherited scripts form us, and it invites readers to question what shaped them without abandoning truth. Awakening is presented not as rebellion, but as a return to what is real.

title: The Step
description: The Step retells Peter’s journey with Jesus through the moments that required movement before certainty. From the first introduction and the empty nets to the storm, the cross, resurrection, and restoration, Peter’s story is told from close range as a life repeatedly pulled between fear, control, loyalty, failure, and trust. The book is about the step that comes when the voice of Jesus calls and obedience must move before understanding catches up.

title: The Signposts of Sin
description: The Signposts of Sin examines how spiritual distance usually begins long before an obvious fall. Drift often starts with a missed whisper, a hesitation, a rationalization, or a small movement away from dependence on God. The book traces stages of deviation and the quiet signposts through which the Spirit calls us back. Its focus is not condemnation, but recognizing the early moments when intimacy begins to fade and learning to return before distance becomes destruction.

title: The Journey Home
description: The Journey Home is a deeply personal exploration of why we were created, what went wrong, and how we return to the life of trust and relationship with God for which we were made. Written in a first-person voice, it moves from self-reliance and striving toward surrender, receiving, freedom, and daily dependence. The book invites readers to recognize their own story in the journey and to stop carrying what God never asked them to carry.

title: Jesus Wants to Kill You: What the Church Neglected to Mention
description: Jesus Wants to Kill You confronts the idea that following Jesus is primarily about improving the old self. The book argues that the gospel goes deeper than self-help, behavior management, or religious performance. Through the language of crucifixion, surrender, demolition, and resurrection, it explores what must die so that the life of Christ can become real in us. The message is intentionally provocative: Jesus does not merely come to make the old life work better. He calls it to the cross.

title: Surely, This Was…
description: Surely, This Was… is a fictional book of truth set in Jerusalem during the final days of Jesus. Told through the perspectives of characters including Simon, Barabbas, Lucius, and Dismas, the story places the reader inside the tension of Roman occupation, Passover, prophecy, violence, doubt, and the unfolding events surrounding the crucifixion. Familiar history becomes personal as ordinary people encounter a moment that will divide time itself.

title: The Unseen Dominion
description: The Unseen Dominion traces the biblical story through the visible and invisible realms, beginning before creation and moving through creation, the fall, Noah, Babel, the patriarchs, Moses, Israel, exile, the Messiah, the cross, and Pentecost. It explores the spiritual beings, divine order, rebellion, conflict, and unseen realities that form the larger biblical backdrop. The result is a sweeping narrative that asks readers to see Scripture as part of a much larger cosmic story.

title: Pre-Form-ing
description: Pre-Form-ing explores how people are shaped before they are fully aware that shaping is happening. Set in a future of emotional systems, predictive technology, and engineered harmony, the story follows the development of tools designed to help people regulate conflict and create safety. As the system succeeds, deeper questions emerge about freedom, friction, authenticity, and what may be lost when human formation becomes too efficient.

title: Mis-Align-ment
description: Mis-Align-ment enters a world where emotional calibration, social harmony, and behavioral resonance have become normal. Grant believes deeply in the system and sees alignment as care, clarity, and peace. But the story begins to expose the tension between order and truth, between externally managed harmony and genuine human freedom. It asks what happens when a system designed to protect people becomes the lens through which every thought, feeling, and relationship is judged.

title: De-Moral-ized
description: De-Moral-ized follows a future world in which language, memory, emotion, and moral judgment are increasingly filtered through systems of resonance and social stability. As Eli begins to notice what has been softened, edited, or forgotten, the story turns toward the recovery of truth, conscience, and memory. The book asks what remains of morality when discomfort is treated as dysfunction and truth must first pass through the test of social harmony.

title: The Scandal of Peace
description: The Scandal of Peace challenges the versions of peace we often settle for: comfort, avoidance, control, numbness, agreement, and the absence of conflict. It explores the deeper peace of Christ, a peace strong enough to hold truth, vulnerability, surrender, pain, and costly reconciliation. The book asks why real peace can feel disruptive when we have built our lives around keeping ourselves safe.

title: The Scandal of Love
description: The Scandal of Love examines the ways love becomes distorted by performance, transaction, fear, control, approval, and the need to be needed. It contrasts these patterns with love as Scripture presents it: beginning in God, moving first, freely given, and impossible to manufacture from the self. The book invites readers to stop trying to earn, manage, or possess love and instead receive the love of God deeply enough that it can flow through them.

title: The Scandal of Grace
description: Grace does not operate by the world’s economy of merit, scarcity, and control. The Scandal of Grace explores a gift that cannot be earned or owned—and why receiving it may be more disruptive than trying to deserve it.

title: The Identity Trap
description: The Identity Trap examines the burden of trying to build, perform, defend, and constantly revise an identity. From labels and wounds to cultural pressure and self-definition, the book traces the voices that tell us who we are and asks the central question: Who gets to name me? It points toward identity as something received from God rather than manufactured from performance, pain, preference, approval, or self-invention.

title: The "What if" Trap
description: The “What If” Trap explores how imagined futures can quietly take control of the present. What-if thinking can look like wisdom and preparation while actually producing fear, hesitation, overthinking, and paralysis. The book examines the illusion of control and offers another way: trusting God for today, receiving present grace, and taking the next faithful step without demanding certainty about everything that comes afterward.

title: The Pride Trap
description: The Pride Trap presents pride not merely as arrogance but as a hidden force that can appear as control, usefulness, fear, self-protection, certainty, busyness, theology, cynicism, and even humility. Structured as a series of confessions, the book exposes the subtle ways pride protects the self and resists surrender. Each confession moves from recognition to unmasking and finally toward the freedom of trusting God instead of maintaining control.

title: The Comparison Trap
description: The Comparison Trap examines the quiet measuring system that turns difference into a judgment of worth. It traces comparison from early formation into adult performance, competition, insecurity, pride, and despair. The book distinguishes healthy recognition of difference from the destructive habit of ranking ourselves against others and points toward a different measure: seeing ourselves through God’s design rather than through the shifting standards of culture.
